overview:
# Case CF-2026-014 — The Missing Research Laptop

**Classification:** Fictional training case  
**Status:** Open  
**Incident date:** 28 October 2026  
**Location:** Meridian Innovation Centre, Building B, Room 204  
**Reported by:** Dr. Meera Sen  
**Estimated property value:** ₹85,000

## Case summary
A university-owned research laptop was reported missing from Room 204 after an afternoon project meeting. Several staff members and students used the room during the day. The available records provide a partial timeline, but there is not enough evidence to identify a person responsible.

## Known facts
- The laptop was reportedly seen on the meeting-room desk at approximately 15:50.
- The room was used for a project meeting between 16:00 and 16:45.
- The reporting person noticed the laptop missing at approximately 18:25.
- The electronic access log records three entries after the meeting.
- A witness recalls seeing someone carrying a dark laptop sleeve, but could not identify the person or confirm the device inside it.

## Persons to clarify / interview
- **Arjun Rao:** Research assistant; attended the meeting.
- **Nisha Kapoor:** Project student; attended the meeting.
- **Facilities staff member:** Accessed the room later in the afternoon; identity to be confirmed.

These are investigative leads only. No evidence in this package establishes guilt.

## Initial investigative priorities
1. Preserve the original access-control log and verify its clock accuracy.
2. Obtain and preserve corridor CCTV footage covering 16:30–18:30.
3. Interview the meeting attendees separately and clarify the last confirmed sighting.
4. Check whether the laptop was moved for maintenance, charging, or safekeeping.
5. Record the device serial number and check authorised asset or repair records.

## Evidence inventory
See `evidence_register.csv` and the five evidence files in `evidence/`.

## Important limitation
This is a fictional, intentionally incomplete case file. The materials contain leads and inconsistencies, not a final finding. Treat each item according to its stated source and reliability.

evidence.reliability_note: Medium; first-hand observation with approximate time
evidence.summary: Laptop reportedly present at 15:50 and missing at 18:25.
evidence.content:
EVIDENCE ITEM: EV-001
TYPE: Witness statement
STATEMENT RECORDED: 28 October 2026, 19:05
WITNESS: Dr. Meera Sen
ROLE: Research supervisor

STATEMENT
I used Room 204 for a project meeting on 28 October. I remember seeing the university laptop on the desk near the display screen at approximately 15:50, before the meeting began. The meeting ended at around 16:45. I left the room shortly afterwards and did not check whether the laptop was still on the desk.

At approximately 18:25, I returned to collect a notebook and noticed that the laptop was no longer there. I asked the office administrator whether it had been moved. No one present could confirm its location.

The laptop is usually stored in a grey sleeve. I cannot say whether the sleeve was present when I returned.

LIMITATIONS
- The 15:50 time is an estimate based on memory, not a timestamped photograph.
- The witness did not observe anyone taking the laptop.
- The witness did not check the desk immediately after the meeting.

RECORDED BY: Case intake officer
STATUS: Statement recorded; witness signature pending

evidence.reliability_note: Medium; system clock not yet independently verified
evidence.summary: Three badge events are recorded after the meeting; badge holder identities require confirmation.
evidence.content:
EVIDENCE ITEM: EV-002
TYPE: Access-control log extract
SOURCE: Meridian Innovation Centre access system
LOCATION: Building B, Room 204
EXPORT TIME: 28 October 2026, 20:10
DATE RANGE: 28 October 2026, 16:30–18:00

EXTRACT
16:52:11 | Badge ID B-104 | Door access granted
17:08:43 | Badge ID B-219 | Door access granted
17:46:02 | Badge ID B-031 | Door access granted

SYSTEM NOTES
- The export contains badge identifiers only; the authorised badge-holder mapping was not included.
- The system clock has not yet been checked against a trusted time source.
- An access-granted event does not prove that the badge holder removed property.
- No door-held-open or forced-entry events appear in this extract.

FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED
Obtain the signed badge-holder mapping from Facilities and preserve the original system export with its audit metadata.

evidence.reliability_note: Low to medium; brief observation, no identification
evidence.summary: Witness recalls an unidentified person carrying a dark laptop sleeve near the corridor around 17:20.
evidence.content:
EVIDENCE ITEM: EV-003
TYPE: Witness statement
STATEMENT RECORDED: 28 October 2026, 19:30
WITNESS: Kavya Iyer
ROLE: Office administrator

STATEMENT
At approximately 17:20, I was near the printer area in the Building B corridor. I noticed a person walking away from the direction of Room 204 while carrying a dark laptop sleeve or a thin document case. I was several metres away and only saw the person briefly.

I cannot identify the person. I did not see the person's face clearly and did not see what was inside the sleeve. I cannot confirm whether the person came from Room 204 or was simply passing through the corridor.

LIMITATIONS
- Approximate time based on memory.
- No identification made.
- Object may not have contained a laptop.
- Direction of travel is uncertain.

RECORDED BY: Case intake officer
STATUS: Statement recorded; witness signature pending

evidence.reliability_note: Medium; record is an email extract, ticket status unverified
evidence.summary: A maintenance request mentions a power socket inspection in Room 204; it does not state that a laptop was removed.
evidence.content:
EVIDENCE ITEM: EV-004
TYPE: Email / maintenance record
SOURCE: Facilities helpdesk mailbox
RECEIVED: 28 October 2026, 16:58
EXTRACTED: 29 October 2026, 09:15

FROM: facilities.helpdesk@example.invalid
TO: building.operations@example.invalid
SUBJECT: Room 204 — socket inspection

Please arrange a check of the wall socket near the presentation desk in Room 204. A user reported intermittent power at the outlet. The room may be accessed after the scheduled meeting if it is free. Please update the ticket once inspected.

TICKET REFERENCE: FAC-204-1028
STATUS IN EXTRACT: Open / completion not recorded

INVESTIGATIVE NOTE
This email establishes that a maintenance request existed. It does not establish that a technician attended, entered the room, handled the laptop, or removed any property. Obtain the full ticket history and technician assignment before drawing conclusions.

NOTE: The email domain is deliberately fictional (.invalid).
